title: How Did Ariana Grande’s ‘Petal’ Album Earn Her Best First-Week Numbers of the Decade?
summary: This week's Five Burning Questions looks at Grande's latest, which bows atop the Billboard 200 this week.
contentText:
While many fans expected 2024’s Eternal Sunshine to be the last new album we got from Ariana Grande in a long while, she’s back atop the Billboard 200 just two and a half years later — and posting some of her strongest numbers yet.

Grande’s eighth solo full-length Petal bows atop the chart with 295,000 first-week units — her best single-week performance of the 2020s thusfar. Meanwhile, it charts all 12 of its tracks in the Billboard Hot 100 ‘s top 40, while notching two songs in the top five: chart-topping lead single “Hate That I Made You Love Me” (No. 2) and the new title track (No. 4), whose video has heated a discourse about the pop star’s physical appearance that has at times threatened to overwhelm the album’s debut week.

How do those Petal numbers compare with our expectations? And will the album era ultimately stand strong on its own? Billboard staffers discuss these questions and more below.

1. Ariana Grande’s  Petal  enters atop the Billboard 200 with 295,000 first-week units — her best single-week performance since  Thank U, Next  in 2019. Is that performance better, worse, or about what you expected from it?

Katie Atkinson:  I don’t know why I would underestimate Ariana Grande at this point in her career, but I think this first week is better than I expected. If you look at the pace of her past two-plus years –  Eternal Sunshine  in March 2024,  Wicked  in November 2024,  Eternal Sunshine 2  in March 2025,  Wicked 2  in November 2025 – it would be easy for an artist to feel overexposed. But then she came back with a new tour and new album this year, and it turns out there was an even bigger appetite for both. You can understand why she would want (and deserves) to step back from the public eye for a minute, and she’s going out on an incredible high.

Kyle Denis : This is around what I expected. I did think she’d be able to break the 300k mark this time around (given the variety of vinyl pressings that were introduced over the past two months), but I wouldn’t be surprised if some listeners were temporarily turned off by the conversation around her spiraling out of control. Considering the darker, more subdued sound of this album — as well as her confrontational lyricism —  Petal  earning Grande her biggest single-week album performance in over seven years is an indisputable win. 

Lyndsey Havens : Better. I would always bet on Ari to secure a No. 1 on the Billboard 200 — in fact, the only solo studio full-length to miss the top spot was  Dangerous Woman , which debuted at No. 2 — and I think since her last album, impressively, interest has only grown. Plus, once you factor in that she called this new album “feral” and made clear she would be talking her s—t, I think that managed to hook her detractors, too, if for nothing more than a curiosity listen. 

Alicia Urrea : I’d say it’s about what I expected, but definitely on the stronger side! Grande is still one of the biggest pop stars in the world, so I personally didn’t doubt a No. 1 debut, but 295,000 units is a particularly massive showing when you consider that the last album of hers to do such strong numbers was  Thank U, Next  in 2019. I wouldn’t necessarily say I expected the equivalent 360,000-unit debut, which was such a huge moment for her, but coming in at 295,000 feels like such a big reflection of how much staying power she still has.

Andrew Unterberger : It’s definitely a little stronger than I expected, but more I’m just a little surprised in retrospect that her last two albums weren’t closer to this unit range. What the hell was Positions doing with a sub-200k first week? She was coming off Thank U, Next !

2. What do you think is the biggest reason for  Petal ’s superior first-week performance to Grande’s last two albums, 2024’s  Eternal Sunshine  (227k) and 2020’s  Positions  (174k)?

Katie Atkinson:  It seems that album sales are the most important factor, including Ari’s biggest-ever week on vinyl. There were a lot of different variants here, as is the norm with an artist of her status, but you can release countless different CDs and records of every color in the rainbow and you’ll still need to have a fanbase who wants to buy them — and she had that in spades. As for promo, I think the Eternal Sunshine Tour that kicked off nearly two months before this album came out was probably the best possible awareness campaign, because Grande was regularly making headlines without doing any interviews or TV appearances.

Kyle Denis : Let’s start with  Positions . First off,  Petal  had the advantage simply by arriving in a year that wasn’t 2020. On a more serious note, I’d bet  Petal  benefited from its two-month pre-order window, while  Positions  likely suffered from the four weeks between the arrival of its lead single and the set’s full release. It also helps that, generally,  Petal  is more pop-forward than  Positions , which matters when your main buyers are a notoriously fickle fanbase. 
 
Now onto  Eternal Sunshine . 227,000 first-week units is nothing to scoff at, but  Eternal Sunshine  pulled those numbers amid arguably Grande’s worst hate train (remember: this was around when news of her Ethan Slater’s relationship first broke) and off the back of a lead single (“Yes, And?”) that came and went with a relative whisper despite reaching No. 1 on the Hot 100. In comparison, Grande has pretty good press leading into  Petal’s  release weekend (the title tack’s music video is what really derailed the conversation) and “Hate That I Made You Love Me” (10) has now spent more weeks in the Hot 100’s top 10 than “Yes, And?” (three) and “We Can’t Be Friends” (six) combined. And, of course, a more somber divorce album was always going to be a tougher commercial sell. 

Lyndsey Havens : She’s back on freaking tour! If you look back on Ariana’s output since her 2013 debut, she has never really gone away. The longest gap between albums is four years, and that was during a pandemic. But in the past few years, she has been more present than ever, with her own music and  Wicked  and her upcoming  Focker-In-Law  film — and, of course, being on tour. She’s stayed top of mind for so long, and gave  petal  a lengthy, somewhat old-school rollout, that interest had strategically peaked just in time for its release.

Alicia Urrea : I think the biggest thing is the amount of steam Grande has built and maintained since  Eternal Sunshine . Between Wicked, her return to the stage and the fact that this is her first major tour in years, she’s had a much bigger presence in pop culture heading into  Petal . The album was also released at a point where fans had been waiting for new music from Grande while actively following her again, so there was a lot of pent-up demand. I think the  Eternal Sunshine  tour also amplified the idea that fans aren’t just listening to  Petal , they’re getting to experience this new era in real time.

Andrew Unterberger : It feels like folks are starting to properly venerate her as a true albums artist. Weird to say about someone who’s been putting out classic LPs basically for a decade now, but it takes a long time as a pop star to divorce yourself from the perception of being primarily a radio hitmaker and establish you’re someone who fans should be plopping down $$$ for to support their full-length projects. Based on these first-week numbers — 168,000 in sales, including 96,000 in vinyl alone — it seems like she’s gotten ther…
